text:
maria: Quick check — ops wants to drop TLS 1.2 from public endpoints next Tuesday. Before we proceed I need confirmation on three things: who owns the cert rotation windows for the public load balancers, whether any internal services still require TLS1.2, and a reminder on the KMS key owners for cert signing (so we can request rotation access).

aj: I can own the LB cert rotation window. planning to do it 03:00-04:00 UTC to minimize traffic.

kevin: Re: internal services — I ran a probe last week but can do a quick sweep. Off the top there are two legacy connectors (payments-legacy, analytics-ingest) that still use clients pinned to TLS1.2. I'll open a small PR to add a handshake-fallback check and schedule them for an upgrade.

maria: Thanks — can you paste the probe command? we should include in the ops runbook.

kevin: Sure: ```bash
# check TLS 1.2 allowed ciphers on host
openssl s_client -connect host.example.com:443 -tls1_2 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject
```

sophie: On approvals: we need security approval + exec sign-off for breaking change. I'm +1 if sec gives the all-clear and we confirm the two legacy services are upgraded or have a canary fallback.

maria: I'll do the security validation. Quick notes:
- Logging: ensure cert/key material is never present in logs during rotation. Ops automation should redact `cert_pem` and `private_key` fields.
- KMS: cert signing key is in AWS KMS alias `alias/redwood-certs-prod` — owners are `kevin` and `maria`. Only those two should be in the rotation access list.

sec-bot: Automated config scan result: latest TLS policy attached to `api-alb` supports TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3. No explicit deny for TLS1.2 found in nginx config on frontends. (scan id: sc-2026-03-xx)

aj: I'll push a small nginx change in infra repo to set `ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;` behind a feature flag and open a PR: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pulls/482

maria: Ping on PR review: @kevin can you review 482 for any downstream impact on internal connectors? need security sign-off after PR merge.

kevin: Reviewing now. If all tests pass I'll approve. Also will add an integration test that runs the `openssl` check against staging in the CI.

sophie: Ops runbook checklist that I'll use during the window:
1) pre-check staging + canary traffic (kevin)
2) notify support + posting banner 30m prior
3) apply TLS config behind flag (aj)
4) rotate certs if needed (aj) — confirm KMS access + no plaintext keys logged (maria)
5) monitor latency/error budget for 30m (sophie)

maria: One more: add a quick grep to the runbook to assert we don't have any `private_key` or `cert_pem` dumps in logs: rg -n "(private_key|cert_pem)" /var/log/* || true — include as step 0.

aj: noted. I'll add the runbook and link it in the PR.

kevin: Approved the PR and added the staging check; will watch the canary during the window.

maria: Security sign-off: we can proceed once the legacy connectors are patched or behind a canary fallback. I'll mark this as authorized for the scheduled window if kevin confirms the upgrades. :thumbsup:

sophie: I'll request Ops access approval ticket tomorrow morning for rotation rights and tag kevin/maria as approvers.

sec-bot: Access request template: `/access-request add ops-user rotate-kms-key alias/redwood-certs-prod reason:\"cert rotation for TLS1.2 deprecation\" approvers:[kevin,maria] expires:24h`

maria: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll close the loop once I see the connectors on the upgrade PRs.

kevin: Follow-up: payments-legacy upgraded to TLS1.3 in branch, analytics-ingest will be ready by EOD. Posting links in the PRs.

sophie: Thanks — leaving a calendar hold for the window and will create the Ops ticket in the morning.

maria: Closing note: remember to scrub any debug logs from the rotation job and to rotate the signing key if there is any accidental exposure. We'll do a post-change audit log check 24h after.
